mappings.note: Contains only the superscription (To the choir director. A Psalm of David). The main text starts in v2.
Contains 'Blessed is he who considers the poor' and 'On the evil day... deliver him'. This corresponds to the second half of OSMAIN v1.
Matches OSMAIN v2: 'The Lord will keep him... make him live... called blessed in the land... do not give him over to his enemies'.
Matches OSMAIN v3: 'The Lord sustains him on the sickbed... you have turned his bed about in sickness'.
Matches OSMAIN v4: 'I said, Lord, be gracious... heal my soul for I have sinned'.
Matches OSMAIN v5: 'My enemies say evil of me... When will he die and his name perish'.
Matches OSMAIN v6: 'If one comes to see me... speaks lies... heart gathers evil... goes out and spreads it'.
Matches OSMAIN v7: 'All who hate me whisper against me... imagine evil for me'.

Contains the quote from OSMAIN v8 ('A deadly plague is poured out on him... he shall not rise again'). However, WLC v9 includes a phrase 'דְּבַר־בְּלִיַּעַל' (a word of Belial/evil) at the start which acts as an introduction to the quote. While OSMAIN v8 starts directly with the content of the plague, the WLC structure here is slightly more explicit about the nature of the speech before quoting it. More importantly, looking closely at the Hebrew text provided: 'דְּבַר־בְּלִיַּעַל יָצוּק בֹּו' (A word of Belial has been poured out on him). OSMAIN v8 says 'En dødelig plage er utøst over ham'. The mapping is effectively exact in meaning, but the WLC verse 9 contains the specific phrase 'word of Belial' which corresponds to 'deadly plague/evil report'. No significant extra content found that isn't covered by OSMAIN's translation choice. Re-evaluating: It matches v8 exactly.
Matches OSMAIN v9: 'Even my close friend... who ate my bread has lifted his heel against me'.
Matches OSMAIN v10: 'But you Lord be gracious... raise me up that I may repay them'.
Matches OSMAIN v11: 'By this I know you delight in me... my enemy will not triumph over me'.
Matches OSMAIN v12: 'In my integrity you have upheld me... set before your face forever'.
Matches OSMAIN v13: 'Blessed be the Lord... from everlasting to everlasting. Amen and amen'.
